You don't need to enter  in the Lower City before completing the search for Bastila, but if you do so before getting Sith papers from Gadon Thek in the Hidden Bek base then you'll be introduced to Mission and Zaalbar outside the  in the west wing. You can also have a first encounter with  outside the Pazaak Room in the east wing, where you can play ../Pazaak/ and wager credits if you bought a card deck in the Upper City cantina, and buy cards to add to that deck.

In the  to the south you can ask Zax to tell you about five bounties, earning experience and collecting credits. Bounty hunting doesn't always move you closer to the dark side of the Force, and sometimes you can even move closer to the light side if you can help your targets instead. You can also sell  to Zax if you have some after returning from the Undercity, moving closer to the dark side of the Force, and earn experience by helping a dancer pass her audition for the  here.

Lower City
You enter from the Lower City at the east end of the ../Pazaak/ room. Javyar's cantina has the same layout as the ../Upper City Cantina/, with four rooms arranged around a central hub. The  is to the south, the  is to the west and the  is to the north.

The Pazaak room upon entry only has two people standing by the Pazaak table in the center of the room, and it isn't really worth speaking to either before buying a Pazaak deck from Garouk in the Upper City cantina. Gelrood, a human male Pazaak player, stands by its northwest corner:

Otherwise:

Uriah, a Twi'lek selling Pazaak cards, stands by its northeast corner to the right of your entry. You can ask him some questions, although this isn't necessary:

Calo Nord
When you reach the threshold of the west exit to the Pazaak room before completing the search for Bastila, you'll witness a brief altercation in the central hub just beyond, between Calo Nord to your left and three Black Vulkars (a Rodian and two Twi'leks) to your right:

|}

Calo Nord throws a grenade, resulting in a blinding flash during which you hear blaster fire. When you can see again, the three Black Vulkars drop dead on the floor, and Calo Nord starts to walk to the exit.

The Black Vulkars may leave remains which can be searched for random content, and you can try speaking to Calo Nord... although you've already seen how that plays out:

Here we go again... choosing the first response at any point from now on will end the dialog without violence:

Persisting may be fun, but it is not a good idea:

|}

At this point, Calo Nord is invulnerable and has : , DC 100, so you cannot possibly win. If you've been silly or inattentive enough to get this far without saving beforehand, you can still save yourself by saving, exiting and then loading the game you've just saved: Calo Nord should now have disappeared.

If you speak to any of the four Lower Taris citizens in the hub of the cantina:

 I can't wait for the big swoop race! I hear the Vulkars have a new engine that's going to break all the records! This gang war is getting out of hand! The Vulkars aren't just attacking the Hidden Beks anymore - they go after everyone! I saw Davik's new starship at the spaceport before the quarantine. They say it's the fastest ship on Taris! He calls it the Ebon Hawk. I heard Davik's hired a Mandalorian mercenary to work for him. I didn't know there were any of them left after the Mandalore wars. Have you got your tickets for Bendak Starkiller's return to the duel ring? I hear it's going to be an illegal death match! Did you hear the news? Gadon Thek is dead! I wonder what's going to happen to the Hidden Beks now?

|}

Bounty Office
The bounty office is off the central hub of the cantina to the south, and you can speak to all its inhabitants. There's a Rodian bounty hunter standing in the northwest corner by a table, and a Twi'lek bounty hunter on the other side of that table by the west wall:

 New face, new face... always new face here! On my world only the strong become trackers. Here everyone is bounty hunter! You new here, take advice. Stay off my contracts! Davik up to something. He bring famous bounty hunter Calo Nord in for a special assignment. Calo no work cheap.

|}

|}

There's a second Twi'lek bounty hunter standing in the southeast corner:

 Zax has started to get stingy... he hasn't added a new freelance contract to the board in nearly a week! I heard Calo Nord is in town. Like there wasn't enough competition in this office already! Now we have the best bounty hunter in the system scooping our contracts! Since the Sith got here the average price for each bounty has gone way up! Davik's had to raise his rates just to compete! Somebody killed Gadon Thek! He didn't even have a bounty on his head - talk about a waste of time! Hey – you're the one who won that swoop race, right? Yeah, I saw the whole thing. And I thought my job was dangerous!

|}

Zax, the Hutt running the bounty office, sits at the back against the south wall:

|}

If you're just looking for information, it'll cost you:

|}

|}

However, he'll tell you about the bounties for free:

|}

You can consult your journal for more details on the bounties, or you can ask Zax:

After being told:

If you ask about a bounty you've already collected:

Return to Zax to collect bounties:

|}

The credits you receive for each bounty depend on how persuasive you can be:

Otherwise:

|}

You'll receive no credits if you fail to persuade him, threaten him and then select the following response:

If you're persuasive you can receive up to 2000 credits for collecting all the bounties (up to 1500 if you're not), although you'll receive less if you help some of the targets instead of killing them. You can move closer to the light or dark side of the Force, and there are opportunities to receive additional experience and credits, as well as items.

All targets can be found in the Lower City apartments and the Upper City, but although you could complete them all before descending to the Undercity, it's advisable to wait until you've completed the search for Bastila, and complete them while escaping Taris (you can collect bounties before agreeing to go with Canderous Ordo to Davik's estate).

Dia's Bounty

|}

Dia can be found in her apartment in the south apartments, your neighbor to the west: if you haven't already met and killed her, you can return to hideout and transit back afterward. You move closer to the dark side of the Force if you kill her (even more so if you threaten her first) but receive some experience for doing so. If you speak to Holdan about it in the  to the north before getting paid by Zax:

|}

Alternatively, if you speak to Holdan about it before killing her:

|}

If you talk to Dia, you'll find Holdan was right about her not having the credits. If you speak to him again:

|}

[passage omitted due to quote overlap]

Otherwise:

If you fail but Bastila is present, she brings the full force of her persuasive powers to bear:

If you follow Holdan to the  and talk to Zax, you'll find that he does indeed stick to his end of the bargain:

Return to Dia to tell her the good news and complete the quest, receiving 125 XP in the process. You can move even closer to the light side of the Force by declining her reward, or you can accept it and receive an .

However it ends, if you speak to Holdan again afterwards:

Matrik's Bounty

|}

Matrik can be found in his apartment in the east Lower City apartments, to the east of the entrance from the Lower City. You can kill him without moving closer to the dark side of the Force, receiving experience and a  from his remains.

Alternatively, you can help him to fake his own death by buying him a permacrete detonator from the  in Upper City South for 50 credits, moving closer to the light side of the Force, receiving 480 XP and allowing you to collect his bounty anyway by lying to Zax:

Selven's Bounty

|}

Selven can be found in her apartment in the west Lower City apartments, to the northeast. This bounty is the most straightforward since there's no way to complete it except killing her, receiving experience and a ,  and  from her remains.

Largo's Bounty

|}

Largo can be found in his apartment in the north apartments, to the east of the entrance from Upper City North. You can extort credits and kill him without moving closer to the dark side of the Force if you don't extort them from him during your first meeting and return to do so more than once (he will then attack you). You receive experience, 50 credits and an  from his remains.

Alternatively, if you have at least 200 credits you can move much closer to the light side of the Force by giving them to him to pay Davik back, receiving 110 XP for this act of generosity but denying yourself the opportunity to collect his bounty:

Bendak's Bounty

|}

Bendak Starkiller appears in the northeast corner of the Pazaak room of the Upper City cantina after you've entered the lobby of its duel ring to the south. However, you cannot kill him there, and to do so you need to enter the ../Duel Ring/ to become Taris Dueling Champion so that he'll come out of retirement to face you in an illegal death match. In the process of becoming champion you'll receive 520 XP and 1500 credits in total. You necessarily move closer to the dark side of the Force by stepping into the arena with him (despite the fact he does so not only voluntarily, but enthusiastically), receiving experience,  from Ajuur and at least 700 credits (900 if you're persuasive, or threaten him to move even closer to the dark side of the Force).

Rakghoul Serum
After speaking to Zelka Forn in the Upper City's  about  and suggesting you might be able to get it, his assistant Gurney mentioned it might be more profitable to deliver it to Zax:

|}

 can be found on the corpse of a Sith Soldier to the south of the Outcast village gate in the Undercity. To minimize travel time, it's best to speak to Zelka on your first visit to the Upper City (you cannot sell it to Zax until Gurney has spoken to you after speaking to Zelka), then wait until you've completed the search for Bastila before returning. You can try to persuade him to give more for it:

Otherwise, you can only make an empty threat about taking your business elsewhere or settle for 1000 credits:

|}

Starlight Entertainers
You'll notice a Twi'lek male and female in the northeast corner of the bounty office, to the left of the entrance, who'll give you an opportunity to receive some easy experience. You don't need to speak to the male, Bib Surool, but if you do so:

Otherwise:

|}

You do need to speak to and persuade the female, Lyn Sekla, to become her partner for her audition, and receive experience if you can get her hired:

|}

Asking how hard it can be always fails, otherwise you can alternate between the other two options until you succeed, since even with 8  and no skill points spent in Persuade you still have 40% chance to do so. However, save game before persuading her, as getting her hired depends on your  and how you choose to dance: you can succeed with as little as 8 Dexterity, even after failing the first two of the three dances, but you can also fail with higher Dexterity, even after succeeding with the first two dances.

Otherwise:

Otherwise:

|}

It doesn’t matter which options you pick for any of the three dances as long as you don’t pick option #3 on your last dance. All other combination of options will result in Lyn passing her audition.

|}

However, you receive nothing if you don't dance well and fall over, or you ruin her audition by taking a dive:

|}

Music Room
The music room is off the central hub of the cantina to the north. Inside a trio of Bith musicians accompany two Twil'ek dancers performing on a stage at the back of the room, but trying to speak to any of them is no more productive than in the Upper City cantina:

 [The musician is too busy playing to pay any attention to you.]

Their audience consists of two Black Vulkars seated to the right of the entrance, neither of whom will comment or engage in dialog, and Holdan, a human male standing to the left whose responses depend on whether your character is male or female:

Despite how this dialog ends you can still speak to him again as though nothing happened. Otherwise, the dialog continues:

If you speak to him again:

|}

If either Zax or Dia herself have told you about Dia's bounty:

Tap Room
The tap room or bar is off the central hub of the cantina to the west. As long as you don't already have Sith papers from Gadon Thek in the Hidden Bek base, Mission will appear outside the tap room to the left, while Zaalbar stands to the right by a table laden with food. As you approach either of them, two Rodians walk out of the tap room and confront Mission:

|}

Mission and Zaalbar will now only remain until you leave the cantina or game (even if you save now, then exit and load the game you've just saved), so if you wish to speak to them once the two Rodians leave and receive a little experience for speaking to Mission, do so now. You can speak to Zaalbar as well, albeit very briefly (get used to this):

Mission is much more talkative, although if you're only interested in receiving experience you can end the dialog at any point and still receive it:

|}

Inside the tap room itself an Aqualish, Bith, Black Vulkar and two Rodians are seated, but none of them will comment or engage in dialog. Only Ja'Gatcha, a two-headed alien standing by the bar in the southwest corner, will speak to you. You don't need to speak to them, but you can ask them about themselves and Taris:

|}

Cockpit, Galaxy Map
After character generation and the opening crawl, you watch the battered freighter with your main character aboard as it drifts towards the ravaged world of Peragus. In its cockpit, a lone Astromech droid is active:

Before you take control of T3-M4, a message pops up:

 Use the left thumbstick to move T3-M4. Swivel the camera with the right thumbstick. Click the right thumbstick to toggle first-person Free Look. Press W, A, S, D (Default) to move T3-M4 and turn. Press Caps Lock (Default) to toggle first-person Free Look. Hold Ctrl (Default) to Look About.

T3-M4 can return to the top right side of the cockpit at any time to Skip Prologue:

The Galaxy Map is on the bottom left side of the cockpit. If you interact with it:

Other than the Ebon Hawk, you can only select Peragus II. However, if you try to travel before completing the prologue:

 You are already at that location. The Ebon Hawk cannot dock with the Peragus Mining Facility until main power has been restored.

As you exit the cockpit via the corridor at its bottom end, a few more messages pop up:

  Journal Entry Added

 The ACTIVE QUESTS screen includes important information related to your ongoing adventures. Refer to this journal for hints and guidance throughout the game.

 [You have new quests. To view your quests, press START to open the Pause Menu and then use the left or right triggers to scroll to the .] [You have new quests. To view your quests, open the Game Menu [Default: ESC] and look in the  (Default: J).]

Even if you Skip Prologue, these quests are completed:

None of the experience received during the prologue is retained by T3-M4 or your main character after skipping or completing it. If you use the Galaxy Map to travel to Peragus II after you actively save the Ebon Hawk, completing the prologue, then none of the items received remains in  for the later use of your main character and party.

However, if you Skip Prologue instead at this point then all items in inventory remain there: this is likely unintentional (and the ../Restored Content Mod/ may change it), but it can be exploited to give you a headstart (albeit unnecessary) on Peragus II.

Communications Console
After exiting the cockpit, if you interact with the main hold door at the bottom end of the corridor:

 [Beyond this door is the main hold of the Ebon Hawk. This door appears to be locked down due to a hull breach. See if there is an emergency override somewhere in the communications room behind you.]

The communications room is back through the doorway in the right side of the corridor:

 This room contains a Plasteel Cylinder and the Communications Console. To target one of these objects, move close to it, or use the left or right triggers to cycle through available targets. To interact with an object, first target it and then press . This room contains a Plasteel Cylinder and the Communications Console. To target one of these objects, move close to it, left click on it, or press Q or E (Default) to cycle through available targets. To interact with an object, first target it and then left click on it.

The communications console is on the right side of the room, directly opposite the doorway:

|}

The plasteel cylinder is to the left of the communications console. If you interact with it, but close it without getting the programming spike inside:

 [Take the programming spike inside this container by pressing . Use this spike to access the terminal nearby.] [Take the programming spike inside this container by clicking on the Get Item button. Use this spike to access the terminal nearby.]

 [You will come across many containers, some of which will be locked. The computer spike you just picked up can be used at computer terminals to access functions such as opening doors.]

You can now use this spike to slice the system and open the main hold door:

|}

Main Hold, Security Console
 This is the Main Hold.

The main hold is the central hub of the Ebon Hawk, and all T3-M4 needs to do is cross it and unlock the low security door in the middle of its bottom wall. If you interact with the door:

 [While some doors can be bashed open (or cut open with a lightsaber or cutting tool), some doors require the use of the  skill to open. Use your Security skill from the action bar to open this door.]

Unlocking it allows access to the bottom half of the vertical corridor between the cockpit and engine room, where you'll also find your main character laying in the . 

There's a red footlocker by the main hold's left wall. If you try to unlock it using the Security skill:

[passage omitted due to quote overlap]

 Some locked doors and containers can be opened by bashing or blasting them with a weapon until they open. Not all doors or containers can be successfully bashed. To bash an object, select it, then select Bash from the TARGET MENU.

T3-M4's unarmed attacks can inflict 1-4 (2.5 average) bludgeoning damage, so on average four hits should bash it open.

 [Sometimes bashing or blowing opening a container will break some of the items in the container. But you can use even broken items. They can be turned into useful components at a workbench.]

These computer spikes can be used to slice the security console in the middle of the main hold:

|}

You can now access security cameras to look around parts of the Ebon Hawk. You can also access security doors to open and close the outer and inner garage doors, but this is pointless while T3-M4 is alone since a hull breach in the garage prevents both doors being open at the same time.

To begin, the outer garage door is open and the inner garage door is closed:

|}

There's a blast door in the top right side of the main hold, and another just inside the corridor exiting its bottom right corner:

 [This blast door is magnetically sealed and cannot be opened.]

This horizonal corridor crosses the main hold, connecting the  on the other side to the starboard dormitory beyond this magnetically sealed blast door. There's a broken droid on the floor here, and another by the bottom left wall:

There's also a body by the bottom right wall:

 [This old woman appears to be dead. There is a keycard on the body that looks like it opens a locker somewhere.] This keycard is used to open up a locker in the storage room.

Medical Room
The bottom half of the vertical corridor between the Ebon Hawk's cockpit and engine room is beyond the low security door in the middle of the main hold's bottom wall. As you exit the main hold:

 [Use the  Screen to help you explore the Ebon Hawk. Press START to open the Pause Menu and then use the left or right triggers to scroll to the Map.] [If you need help exploring the Ebon Hawk, access the  screen by pressing M (Default).]

The medical room is beyond another low security door in the left wall of this corridor, on your right as you go down it.

 This is the Medical Room.

Your main character lies on a bed by its top wall:

There's a medical storage bin beside the bed, in the top left corner:

T3-M4 can now use one of these on your main character, although this is a bonus mission which doesn't need to be completed to complete the prologue:

Lift to Outside the Ebon Hawk
There's a lift opposite the medical room, in the right wall of the corridor between the main hold and the engine room:

 This is the Utility Lift.

The engine room door is at the bottom end of this corridor, just beyond a junction:

 This is the Engine Room.

If you interact with it:

 [This door is damaged and cannot be opened with your Security skill, or by bashing it. You will have to find and use an explosive trap to open this door. Take the lift outside the Ebon Hawk to find one.]

Return to the lift and use its controls to go outside:

The lift  takes T3-M4 up to the middle of the Ebon Hawk's exterior hull, just below its gun turret.

Starboard Outer Hull
T3-M4 has already started going down a ramp onto the Ebon Hawk's starboard side, to the right of the lift controls.

 This is the Starboard side of the Ebon Hawk.

Below the ramp on your right, there's a busted port in the starboard engine:

 [This busted engine port has some needed Parts for the Ebon Hawk's hyperdrive. Take the Parts here back down below to get main power restored.]

There's an open hatch in the floor below this port, to your left, another two open hatches out on the starboard side opposite the ramp down, and one more above the ramp, next to the cockpit:

 [This open hatch has some Parts that will be useful for getting main power restored.]

There's also some exposed wiring in the top right of the starboard side:

Port Outer Hull
As you return to the lift controls from the starboard outer hull:
 Don't forget to explore the other side of the Ebon Hawk.

You need to go down a ramp onto the port side:

 This is the Port side of the Ebon Hawk. 

Proton Missile, Mines
There's an unstable proton missile embedded in the bottom left of the port side, below the ramp:

Getting too close and triggering these can damage but not kill T3-M4. Otherwise, with  on Easy or Normal they can be disabled or recovered, but on Difficult they can only be disabled, not recovered. However, one can always be recovered from the proton missile itself:

 [You can use the explosive device in this missile to blow open the engine room door inside the Ebon Hawk. This will give you access to the hyperdrive. After you plant a mine, back away quickly so that you do not take damage.]

If T3-M4 sets mines until there are none in :

 If you run out of mines, you can return to the Proton Missile and collect another.

Quadlasers
There are damaged quadlasers on the top left of the port side, slightly above the ramp.

 [This is one of the Ebon Hawk's quadlaser turrets. They are damaged, but you can scavenge some Parts from it to use in repairing the Ebon Hawk.]

Lift to Inside the Ebon Hawk
Return to the lift controls in the middle of the outer hull once T3-M4 has at least one  from the starboard side, and at least five  in :

Engine Room, Hyperdrive
Once you have a  from the starboard side of the Ebon Hawk's starboard outer hull, you can go back inside to the engine room door at the bottom end of the corridor and use a mine to open it:

 [This door is damaged and cannot be opened with your Security skill, or by bashing it. You can use a mine to open this door. Once you plant the mine, back away from the door to avoid taking damage.]

If T3-M4 sets the mine(s) in the corridor until none are in :

 If you run out of mines, you can return to the Proton Missile outside the Ebon Hawk and collect another.

Recover the mine(s), then select the engine room door before using one:

 Left-clicking the mouse while a mine is selected in your ACTION MENU will place a mine. You can also disable and recover enemy mines and add them to your own inventory for later use.

T3-M4 takes no damage even if you don't back away, but the blast opens the door. Inside the engine room, the port and starboard engines are to either side:

 [The port engine is shut down, but appears intact. Fixing the hyperdrive will allow you to restore power to the port engine and bring primary power online.] [The Starboard engine is badly damaged. Fixing it won't be possible until after docking with the Peragus mining station.]

The hyperdrive is at the bottom end of the engine room:

[passage omitted due to quote overlap]

 [The port engine is powered up. You can now use the Galaxy Map to travel to the Peragus mining station.]

You can now return to the cockpit to complete the prologue, using the Galaxy Map to travel to the ../Peragus II/ mining station:

 This is the Cockpit.

The Galaxy Map is on the bottom left side:

Otherwise, you can still skip the prologue there, or explore the optional areas of the Ebon Hawk (if you haven't already done so).

Cargo Hold
The corridor to the left of the junction between the engine room and the main hold has a low security door in its left outer wall. If you interact with this door:

 [While some doors can be bashed open (or cut open with a lightsaber or cutting tool). Some doors require the use of the  skill to open. Use your Security skill from the action bar to open this door and search the remains of the cargo hold beyond.]

 This is the Cargo Hold.

This cargo hold has the droid 3C-FD in its bottom corner, opposite the doorway, and a locker by its right wall:

 [This container is locked and requires a key. Search the ship to find the key to this locker.]

The locker key is found on the body by the bottom right wall back in the .

 [You used the keycard you found to open the locker. The Impact Armor from this locker can be equipped on the  Screen. Press START to open the Pause Menu and then use the left or right triggers to cycle to the Equip screen.] [You used the keycard you found to open the locker. The Impact Armor from this locker can be equipped on the  Screen. To open the Equip screen, click on the Blaster icon in the top right area of the screen or press U (Default).]

There's a high security cylinder in the hold's top left corner, with an unlocked plasteel cylinder next to it.

Changing  to Difficult increases the lock's Difficulty Class by 5, to 41 (while changing to Easy decreases it by 5, to 31, which is still too difficult to open):

 [You must lower your difficulty setting in order to open this lock. Access the  screen and select Gameplay. Then change the difficulty setting from Difficult to Normal.] [The lock on this container is too difficult to open. You'll need to use a security tunneler to help open the lock. Look in the unlocked cylinder next to this one to find security tunnelers.]

 [If you encounter a difficult lock on a container or door, you can use a security tunneler on it to improve your chance of opening the lock. Use the security tunneler to open the High Security Cylinder nearby.]

Returning to the high security cylinder:

[passage omitted due to quote overlap]

 You can have multiple powers or items in each icon of the ACTION MENU. Scroll up or down using the mouse wheel to cycle through the various options.

Combat Training
There's a metal box in the middle of the cargo hold which can be unlocked for combat training:

 [You can equip a weapon from the  screen. Press START to open the Pause Menu, and then use the left or right triggers to cycle to the Equip screen.] [You can equip a weapon from the  screen. To open the Equip screen, click on the Blaster icon in the top right area of the screen or press U (Default).]

If you interact with any of the four sensor droids before equipping a weapon:

 [T3-M4 must equip a blaster before attacking the sensor droids. Press START to open the Pause Menu and then use the left or right triggers to cycle to the Equip screen.] [T3-M4 must equip a blaster before attacking the sensor droids. To open the Equip screen, click on the Blaster icon in the top right area of the screen or press U (Default).]

If you open the metal box again:

 [Destroy all the sensor balls to continue to the next step of combat training.]

Once T3-M4 has equipped a Field Survival Pistol:

 ENEMY SIGHTED!Press the Pause key (SPACE or Pause) to continue

 The game pauses when you sight an enemy, and the selection reticle will show up in red. You can use the mouse to select other hostile targets. This auto-pause option can be disabled on the  screen.

 [Change your target by using the left and right triggers. To attack an enemy, select the Sword icon with the D-pad and press . To queue up multiple combat actions, press . To cancel the last combat action, press .] [Change your target by pressing Q or E, or left click on the object you want to target. To attack an enemy, left click on the Sword icon or press 1. To Queue up actions, left click multiple times. Clear your last combat action by clicking in the queue, or by pressing Y.]

The sensor droids cannot attack or inflict damage. If you attack a sensor droid:

 ../Combat/ mode engaged

 Whenever you spot an enemy, left-click the selected enemy once to enter combat mode. This will lock the camera on your selected target. Left-clicking the target again causes your character to perform the Default Action and attack each round. Your chances of hitting a target are controlled by your statistics and behind the scenes combat rolls. Combat is not affected by your aim, your character's movements or the movements of your target.

 Remember: Only left-click the targetted enemy ONCE to engage. You will automatically attack your target each round. You do not have to left-click it again until you select a new target. When engaged in combat you can use the TARGET and ACTION MENUs to activate items, feats and Force powers each round. Otherwise your character will automatically perform their default attack each round.

Sensor droids only have 8  and 1 , so they're easy to hit and any damage inflicted will destroy them. Once the first group has been destroyed:

You're outnumbered five to one, with three in front and two behind, but from the dismissive reaction if you lose, you'd think those odds were reversed:

If it taking more than two of them to defeat a single low-to-mid-level Jedi without a lightsaber hasn't taught them humility, then maybe only defeating all five will do so (although refusing a rematch may be taken as a tacit admission of that being possible).
